details.groundedness_reasoning:
1. A positive perfect square is the square of an integer n. If n = 1, the square is 1, which is not prime because primes must be greater than 1. If n > 1, n² is a product of two smaller natural numbers, n and n, so it is not prime.
2. Thus the definitions in citation [4] establish the gold target claim that no prime number is a square. Consequently, no sum of two prime numbers that are both perfect squares exists.
